Pull Over, Pull Up & the rest

Small words, big difference. Learn how English builds movement, then watch it happen on the street below.

Verb + Direction
The formula behind every movement phrase

In English, most driving movements aren't one word — they're a movement verb plus a small direction particle. The verb alone barely means anything here; the particle is what tells you where.

pull / drive / back / speed / slow + over / up / into / out / around / away = meaning

Change the particle, change the meaning completely — even though the verb stays the same.

Speaker trap

"Pull" is not "puxar" here. Nothing is being pulled. If you translate these phrases word-for-word into Portuguese, none of them make sense — you have to learn the whole phrase as one unit, not the words separately.

PhraseLiteral (wrong)Real meaning
Pull over"puxar por cima"Encostar e parar no acostamento
Pull up"puxar para cima"Chegar e parar em frente a um lugar
Pull into"puxar para dentro"Entrar (garagem, vaga, posto)
Pull out"puxar para fora"Sair de onde estava parado
Pull away—Arrancar, sair andando depois de parado
